To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fracture toughness of unidirectional carbon fiber/epoxy composites under Mode I, Mode II, and mixed Mode I/II (in the ratio of 3/4) loadings were determined and the fracture toughness data were shown to fit a simple failure criterion.

(a) the fracture toughness data for IM7/977 -1 composite under mixed mode loading were found to fit the power law failure criterion; (b) the pre-cracking of IM7/977 composite prior to the fracture toughness testing is essential for the accurate measurement of fracture toughness; (c) the fracture toughness values of IM7/97 7 - 1 composite under Mode I, Mode II, and mixed Mode I/ Mode II loadings were found to increase as the crack

the fracture toughness of the IM7/977–1 composite under mixed mode loading is lower than that under pure Mode I and Mode II loading and that the fracture toughness under Mode I and mixed mode loadings is lower than that of pure Mode II loading.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fracture behaviour of a carbon fibre/epoxide composite in mixed mode loading conditions.
the fracture of unidirectional carbon-fibre/epoxy composites under Mode I, Mode II, and mixed-mode loading conditions.
the development of a fracture toughness testing method for unidirectional composites under mixed mode I and II loadings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fracture toughness data of the UD composite can be predicted from the Mode I data using a simple power law criterion.

the delamination failure resistance of UD composite is a complex function of the applied load mode, the fibre/matrix interfacial properties, the matrix toughness, the fibre volume fraction, and the fibre/matrix debonding and frictional properties.
the fracture toughness of UD composites is dependent on the loading mode and that a simple failure criterion can describe the fracture toughness data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the delamination resistance of UD carbon fibre/epoay composite is strongly dependent on the loading mode.

the fracture behaviour of UD composite is governed by the fibre/matrix interface and the fracture toughness is a function of the fibre/matrix shear strength, the matrix fracture toughness and the fibre/matrix debond length.

The main takeaway from our work is that
Mode II fracture toughness data can be obtained from the same UD beam used for Mode I fracture toughness testing.

the fracture toughness data for the UD composite can be used to predict the onset of delamination under complex loading conditions, such as the ones encountered in the manufacture of composite structures by autoclaving.
the fracture toughness of the UD composite is not only dependent on the mode of loading but also the loading ratio between Mode I and Mode II.
